text:
Forensic findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: An institutional records office accepts intake documentation through designated submission channels, each assigned a reference number at the point of entry. Files are indexed by case type, date, and responsible party, and are retained according to a fixed schedule before archival or certified destruction. Access to non-public records is role-restricted; retrieval, amendment, and release are logged in an audit trail capturing actor identifier, timestamp, record version, and action type. Periodic audits reconcile the audit trail against retention schedules and sample records for integrity. Ordinary paperwork — forms, correspondence, ledgers, and transactional records — moves between departments via stamped transfer slips, and any deviation from standard fields (blank, overwritten, or unexplained entries) is flagged for manual review. The office treats the audit trail as the primary evidentiary substrate: conduct is reconstructed from what the trail shows, not from what any individual asserts.

2) What occurred: The actor produced an intake document dated within the period under review, recorded in the office's case-intake register under a criminal-matter reference number. The intake document contained a free-text request field in which the actor entered a statement referencing an upcoming trial, a target decision (acquittal), and four enumerated objectives. No supporting documentation, no counsel of record, and no prior case linkage were attached to the intake file. The intake was routed by the standard triage channel to the responsible reviewer; the reviewer's acknowledgement field was completed the same day. No amendment to the intake document was recorded in the audit trail between intake and the period under review. The register entry shows a single actor identifier associated with the submission channel used, consistent with a direct, non-mediated filing.

3) Materials/access observed: The intake register entry; the intake document in free-text format with the request field populated; the triage routing slip bearing the same date and reference number; the reviewer's acknowledgement field in the workflow log; the audit-trail excerpt covering the intake window, showing one submission event and one acknowledgement event, with no intervening edits. No secondary documents, attachments, or related reference numbers appear in the file index for the same actor identifier during the window.

4) Indicators & artifacts: A free-text intake field containing multi-part objectives that exceed the scope of ordinary case administration; absence of any attached supporting record, representation, or prior reference despite the stated procedural stage; a single-event audit trail (submission plus acknowledgement only) with no amendments or follow-up entries; a routing path terminating in reviewer acknowledgement without escalation to the standard referral queue; and a file index showing no companion documents for the actor identifier within the period. Together, these artifacts allow an auditor to bound the scope of the filing and to distinguish a standard intake from one that warrants expanded review under the office's deviation-flagging policy.
